source_title: Amy Davidson Reveals What John Ritter Whispered to Her at Their First Table Read (Exclusive) - People.com
source_excerpt:
Davidson says the later Ritter’s encouragement inspires her as she returns to acting after focusing on motherhood
Ron Tom/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty
Amy Davidson says John Ritter praised her talent during their first 8 Simple Rules table read
Ritter played Davidson and Kaley Cuoco’s father before his sudden death during the show’s second season
Davidson says his encouragement still inspires her as she returns to acting after focusing on motherhood
Amy Davidson is remembering her 8 Simple Rules co-star John Ritter .
Davidson starred as Kerry Hennessy on the ABC sitcom alongside Kaley Cuoco, who played her sister Bridget, from 2002 to 2005.
Ritter famously played the two women’s overbearing father Paul Hennessy before his sudden tragic death at the age of 54 from aortic dissection during the second season of the show.

Speaking to PEOPLE in a recent exclusive interview, Davidson, 47, said of her former on-screen dad: “He left such a deficit.”
She went on to recount her first interaction with Ritter, during a pre-table read for 8 Simple Rules.
“It was the first time we met John and Katey [Sagal, who played her mom] ‘cause the kids were cast first,” she said. “I was so nervous. And then John and I sat next to each other at the table, and in the pilot, I had an emotional scene, and I just give it my all because it’s a table read and whatever, I go there emotionally, and he grabbed my hand under the table, and he whispered in my ear, ‘You’re so f---ing talented.’”
The moment is one that’s stuck with her, she says.
“When I doubt myself ... I have that whisper in my ear,” Davidson says.
Having stepped back from the industry in recent years, Davidson says she’s struggled with balancing life as a mom with her passion for acting.
“I’ve been complacent with a lot of life and just dove into my son’s life ... But as he’s getting older, I’m like, ‘Okay, I need to get back to me. That’s important too,’ ” she acknowledges.
She continues: “And it was not easy to get pregnant, and I just have felt like he’s the biggest gift I’ve ever received, but I also know I’m here on earth to be a storyteller, so I’ve had this conflict for many years.”

Those early words of wisdom from the late Ritter, she says, continue to hum in her ears.
“I’m just like, ‘You know what, it’s time to focus on me,’ and I can hear John, you know,” she muses. “I’m definitely very lucky to have him as an angel, but again, I hate that he’s not here.”
